Solve the following problem as completely as you can.

<problem>
A finite set $A\subset\mathbb Z$ is Sidon if all differences $a-a'$ with $a\ne a'$ in $A$ are distinct. It extends to a perfect difference set modulo $v$ if $A\subseteq B$ for some finite $B\subset\mathbb Z$ whose elements are pairwise distinct mod $v$ and in which every nonzero residue class mod $v$ is $b-b'$ for exactly one ordered pair $(b,b')$ of distinct elements of $B$. Is it true that every Sidon set $A\subset\mathbb N$ with $|A|=4$ extends to a perfect difference set modulo some $v>0$? If so, is $v=q^2+q+1$ with $q$ a prime power always possible? If not, what is the least $k$ such that some Sidon set of size $k$ does not extend? ($\{1,2,4,8,13\}$ shows $k\le5$.)
</problem>
